```{python}
#| label: setup
import pandas as pd
import pyreadstat
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io as pio

# ── Brand palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PALETTE = ["#7BB3B2", "#65A6BD", "#C997AF", "#B8B0D3",
           "#F4CF97", "#98B9A0", "#F6DECD"]

# ── Plotly template ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
_tpl = go.layout.Template()
_tpl.layout = go.Layout(
    font=dict(family="Roboto, sans-serif", size=13, color="#333"),
    title_font=dict(size=16, color="#104C52"),
    plot_bgcolor="white",
    paper_bgcolor="white",
    colorway=PALETTE,
    xaxis=dict(showgrid=False),
    yaxis=dict(showgrid=True, gridcolor="lightgray", gridwidth=0.5),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="left", x=0),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=60, b=40),
)
pio.templates["brand"] = _tpl
pio.templates.default = "brand"

# ── Toolbar config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PLOTLY_CONFIG = {
    "displaylogo": False,
    "modeBarButtonsToRemove": ["select2d", "lasso2d", "autoScale2d"],
    "toImageButtonOptions": {"format": "png", "width": 1200, "height": 700, "scale": 2},
}
```

```{python}
#| label: load-data
df, metadata = pyreadstat.read_sav("../../data/zambia/ZM_LFS_DATASET2024_Annual_10percent.sav")

vvl = metadata.variable_value_labels  # value labels lookup

# Decode categorical columns used throughout
df["gender"]    = df["A2"].map(vvl["A2"])
df["education"] = df["B6"].map(vvl["B6"])
df["province"]  = df["PROV"].map(vvl.get("PROV", {})).fillna(df["PROV"].astype(str))
```

## Introduction

This report summarises key findings from the **Zambia Labour Force Survey 2024**.
It covers the demographic profile of the survey population — age structure,
gender balance, education attainment, and a provincial breakdown — based on the
annual 10 % sample.

::: {.callout-note}
All charts are based on unweighted sample counts unless stated otherwise.
:::

---

## Demographics

### Age Distribution

The survey covers respondents across a wide age range. The histogram below shows how the sample is distributed by single year of age, with a dashed line marking the median.

```{python}
#| label: fig-age-hist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of respondent ages with median reference line"

age = df["A3"].dropna()
median_age = age.median()

fig = go.Figure(
    go.Histogram(x=age, nbinsx=20, marker_color=PALETTE[0], name="Age")
)
fig.add_vline(
    x=median_age, line_dash="dash", line_color="red",
    annotation_text=f"Median: {median_age:.0f}",
    annotation_position="top right",
)
fig.update_layout(title="Age Distribution", xaxis_title="Age", yaxis_title="Count")
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

### Population Pyramid

Breaking the age distribution down by gender reveals the demographic structure of the sample. Each bar represents a five-year cohort, with males shown to the left and females to the right.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pyramid
#| fig-cap: "Age pyramid by five-year cohort"

bins       = list(range(0, 85, 5))
age_labels = [f"{b}–{b+4}" for b in bins[:-1]]

pyr = df[["gender", "A3"]].dropna().copy()
pyr["age_group"] = pd.cut(pyr["A3"], bins=bins, labels=age_labels, right=False)

male   = pyr[pyr["gender"] == "Male"].groupby("age_group", observed=True).size()
female = pyr[pyr["gender"] == "Female"].groupby("age_group", observed=True).size()

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    y=age_labels,
    x=-male.reindex(age_labels, fill_value=0).values,
    name="Male", orientation="h", marker_color=PALETTE[0],
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    y=age_labels,
    x=female.reindex(age_labels, fill_value=0).values,
    name="Female", orientation="h", marker_color=PALETTE[2],
))
fig.update_layout(
    title="Age Pyramid",
    xaxis_title="Population Count",
    barmode="overlay",
    bargap=0.1,
    height=600,
)
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

### Gender Split

The donut chart below shows the overall share of male and female respondents in the sample.

```{python}
#| label: fig-gender
#| fig-cap: "Share of respondents by gender"

gender_counts = df["gender"].value_counts()

fig = go.Figure(go.Pie(
    labels=gender_counts.index,
    values=gender_counts.values,
    hole=0.4,
    marker=dict(colors=PALETTE[:2], line=dict(color="white", width=1.5)),
    textinfo="percent+label",
))
fig.update_layout(title="Population by Gender")
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

## Education

### Highest Level Completed

The chart below ranks education levels by the number of respondents who report each as their highest completed qualification, from least to most common.

```{python}
#| label: fig-education
#| fig-cap: "Number of respondents by highest completed education level"

edu = df["education"].value_counts().sort_values()

fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(
    y=edu.index, x=edu.values, orientation="h",
    marker_color=PALETTE[0],
    text=edu.values, textposition="outside",
))
fig.update_layout(
    title="Highest Education Level Completed",
    xaxis_title="Number of respondents",
    height=max(400, len(edu) * 32),
)
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

### Education by Gender — Summary Table

The table below cross-tabulates education level against gender, showing absolute counts and a row total. Rows are sorted by total respondents in descending order.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-education-gender
#| fig-cap: "Respondent counts by education level and gender"

pivot = (
    df.dropna(subset=["education", "gender"])
    .pivot_table(index="education", columns="gender", aggfunc="size", fill_value=0)
    .assign(Total=lambda d: d.sum(axis=1))
    .sort_values("Total", ascending=False)
    .reset_index()
)

cols   = list(pivot.columns)
header_vals = [c if c != "education" else "Education level" for c in cols]

# Alternate row fill for readability
n_rows    = len(pivot)
fill_odd  = ["#f0f8f8"] * n_rows   # light teal tint
fill_even = ["white"]   * n_rows
row_fills = [fill_odd[i] if i % 2 == 0 else fill_even[i] for i in range(n_rows)]

fig = go.Figure(go.Table(
    columnwidth=[250] + [80] * (len(cols) - 1),
    header=dict(
        values=[f"<b>{h}</b>" for h in header_vals],
        fill_color="#104C52",
        font=dict(color="white", size=13),
        align=["left"] + ["center"] * (len(cols) - 1),
        height=36,
    ),
    cells=dict(
        values=[pivot[c].tolist() for c in cols],
        fill_color=[row_fills] * len(cols),
        font=dict(color="#333", size=12),
        align=["left"] + ["center"] * (len(cols) - 1),
        height=30,
    ),
))
fig.update_layout(
    title="Education Level by Gender",
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=60, b=10),
    height=80 + len(pivot) * 32,
)
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```

### Education by Gender — Crosstab

The same data as a formatted crosstab, with row percentages in parentheses.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-crosstab
cross = pd.crosstab(df["education"], df["gender"], margins=True, margins_name="Total")

pct = cross.div(cross["Total"], axis=0).mul(100).round(1)
display = cross.copy().astype(object)
for col in [c for c in cross.columns if c != "Total"]:
    display[col] = cross[col].astype(str) + " (" + pct[col].astype(str) + "%)"

display.style.format(na_rep="—")
```

## Provincial Profile

The sample spans all provinces of Zambia. The chart below shows how respondents are distributed across provinces, which reflects both population size and sampling design.

```{python}
#| label: fig-province
#| fig-cap: "Sample size by province"

prov_counts = df["province"].value_counts().sort_values()

fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(
    y=prov_counts.index, x=prov_counts.values, orientation="h",
    marker_color=PALETTE[1],
    text=prov_counts.values, textposition="outside",
))
fig.update_layout(
    title="Respondents by Province",
    xaxis_title="Count",
    height=max(350, len(prov_counts) * 36),
)
fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG)
```
